newsitem.title: EGYPT: CIB 300 mln pound bond offer opens May 4.
newsitem.headline: CIB 300 mln pound bond offer opens May 4.

text.p: Commercial International Bank (CIB) in Egypt said on Thursday it was offering 300 million pounds ($88.4 million) in bonds from May 4.

The five-year, floating rate notes will be in units of 1,000 pounds and the fee will be three pounds per note. They will be offered for at least ten days and up to two months, or until the issue is covered.
The bonds pay every six months. The rate will be fixed on the average annual return on 182-day treasury bills within 14 days before cashing the coupon plus one-eighth percent.
If the treasury does not issue 182-bills, the rate will be calculated on the loan or discount rate minus three percent but not less than nine percent.
The bank will issue them in lots of one, five, 10, 25, 50 100 and 500 notes, the statement in Al-Ahram newspaper said.

CIB is Egypt's largest private-sector bank and the only one with shares traded internationally. In January its shareholders gave the board clearance to raise up to 900 million pounds ($265 million) by issuing pound or foreign currency bonds or floating-rate notes over two years.
The statement said CIB profits were 181 million pounds as of September 30, 1996. Shareholders' equity was 963 million pounds.
It said that the bank expected net profits to rise to 299 million pounds in 1998 from an expected 267 million pounds in 1997. It saw profits rising to 419 million pounds in 2002.
